elements.texte:
[cheerful] Here’s what happened, in slow motion.

Léa Simon checks availability: 1 spot.

Nathan Petit checks availability: 1 spot.

Léa Simon starts her enrollment.

Nathan Petit starts his before Léa Simon’s is finished.

Both enrollments are recorded in the enrollments table.

Each one gets a confirmation for the last spot.

Your turn!

The spots left go to minus 1: one spot was booked twice.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] A transaction groups a booking’s changes.

Isolation governs what transactions can see and do while they run at the same time.

Here’s Léa Simon’s booking, in a transaction.

Select for update reads the spots and locks the workshop’s row.

The lock is held until the end of the transaction.

The INSERT records the enrollment, and the UPDATE removes a spot.

COMMIT commits the booking and releases the lock.
elements.apres: Let’s replay the two bookings, with the lock this time.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Let’s replay the two bookings, with the lock this time.

Click “Book my spot” on Léa Simon’s phone.

Léa Simon starts her transaction.

She locks the workshop’s row and checks there’s a spot left.

Nathan Petit tries to book.

Your turn!

His transaction waits until it can lock that same row.

His screen shows “Checking availability…”.

Léa Simon records her enrollment.

Your turn!

The number of spots goes from 1 to 0.

Léa Simon commits with COMMIT.

Her enrollment is confirmed and the lock is released.

Nathan Petit can check availability in turn.

There are 0 spots left: no enrollment is created for him.

The lock stops the two bookings from changing this workshop’s availability at the same time.

Nathan Petit checks the spots after Léa Simon’s transaction ends.
elements.avant: COMMIT commits the booking and releases the lock.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] What if Léa Simon’s transaction were rolled back with ROLLBACK?

Let’s go back to just before her COMMIT: the row is still locked.

Your turn!

ROLLBACK rolls back her enrollment and releases the lock.

The spot stays available.

Nathan Petit can then book it.
elements.avant: Nathan Petit checks the spots after Léa Simon’s transaction ends.
elements.apres: With a lock, a booking waits its turn or goes ahead.

[cheerful] With a lock, a booking waits its turn or goes ahead.

Your turn!

A transaction alone isn’t enough to avoid every conflict.

The isolation level and the mechanisms used, like locks, determine how simultaneous access is handled.

In the next lesson, you’ll store routines and calculations in the database.
